Committee: Children, Youth and Human Services
Sponsor: Jones
Analyst: Tiffany Weaver
Date: 01/12/2022
FISCAL NOTE
Senate Bill 31 as introduced could increase the personnel costs of affected state agencies in the event that a state employee who would have exhausted all available leave is able to remain on payroll as a result of receiving donated annual leave, compensatory leave or sick leave. The amount of the increased obligation is undetermined but would be dependent upon the number of state employees who adopt a child and the amount of leave donated to state employees for this purpose.
Andrew Jones, Chairperson
Children, Youth and Human Services

Committee: Ways and Means General Fund
Sponsor: Sorrell
Analyst: JT Mathis
Date: 01/24/2022
FISCAL NOTE
House Bill 127 as introduced exempts virtual currency from ad valorem taxation. Virtual currency is not subject to ad valorem tax, and due to this, this bill will not directly affect state or local funding.
Steve Clouse, Chair
Ways and Means General Fund
